methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $84M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
LuxWall is a Series B climate and energy technology company founded by Scott Thomsen that has raised $84M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private firms and 1 public company (LNZA) in the climate and energy sector, with particular focus on three same-sector, adjacent-stage peers: KoBold Metals ($3.0B, Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B, Series C), and Amogy ($700M, Series C).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $84M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier, implies a valuation of $160M. The peer-median method, grounded in the three comparable company valuations above, yields a median implied value of $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B. These methods produce materially different outputs, reflecting both the early-stage nature of LuxWall relative to its Series C comparables and the wide dispersion in climate-tech valuations at this stage.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $136M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $580M. The significant spread between methods—particularly the gap between stage-progression ($160M) and peer-median ($1.0B) results—reflects uncertainty around LuxWall's competitive positioning within the peer set and the extent to which it commands a valuation premium or discount relative to its Series C-stage comparables.
